gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at maker-store prices on 2026-11-11, the INIU SnapGo Air ($54.99) undercuts the Baseus PicoGo AM52 with cable ($55.99) by $1 while Macworld lists it at 39.2 Wh against 36 Wh and 185% against 182% in its recharge test, or that the Anker MagGo 2 Pro ($109.99) costs $54 more than the Baseus for 17 more points in that test.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited, updated Oct 5, 2026) and Anker's Qi2 25W blog (Sept 18, 2026). Macworld already prints the per-model Wh, weight, thickness and recharge score, so the raw ingredients are there. It lacks today's maker-store prices (it shows the Baseus at $59.99 on Amazon), any cost-per-recharge figure, the INIU SnapGo Compact at $44.99, and the Baseus AM61. Anker's blog covers only Anker models and gives no prices. The Verge, TechRadar and pickedtech pages could not be read (blocked, truncated, TLS error), so the score stays at 1 rather than 2.
decides: It confirms the Baseus PicoGo AM52 with cable as a value pick at $55.99, about half the Anker's price, but it does not make it a clear winner. On Macworld's figures the INIU SnapGo Air is $1 cheaper, thinner (13.7 mm vs 16 mm), holds 3.2 Wh more and has the same 45 W wired output; the AM52's only sourced edge is a smaller footprint (102 × 67 mm vs 105 × 71 mm). The Anker MagGo 2 Pro stays the pick only when the fan and the 199% score are worth $54 more. The UGREEN pick could not be priced today.
